reading.body:
Browser-use alone accounts for 111,761 stars out of 287,381 total across five repositories, making web-automation the dominant attractor in this category by a wide margin over any single coding tool.

The five repositories split cleanly into two functions: three assist with writing or editing code inside a terminal or IDE, and two give AI agents control of a browser to automate tasks on the web. All five are actively maintained, with four showing commits within the final days of August 2026. None is archived. The licensing is entirely permissive, three under Apache-2.0 and two under MIT, which removes legal friction from embedding these tools in larger systems.

For AI infrastructure, the significance is indirect but real. Coding agents that generate, review, and refactor software accelerate the rate at which new model training pipelines, data tooling, and deployment infrastructure can be built and iterated. Browser agents extend that reach to any web-based workflow. Higher development velocity means more compute-intensive workloads reaching production faster, which tightens demand on the power and data-center capacity that sit upstream.

The data covers only GitHub star counts, licences, languages, and activity dates. It does not show adoption inside enterprises, the models these tools call, the compute cost of running them at scale, or how usage has changed over time. Star counts reflect developer interest, not deployment volume.
